Question_text: The apparatus shown in Fig. 1.1 is used to measure the extension of a spring. The cyclist leaves town A at time t = 0 and arrives at town B at t = 4.0 hours.
image: Fig. 1.1 shows a vertical spring with a mass hanging from its bottom end. A vertical scale is placed next to the spring to measure its length/extension. The top of the spring is attached to a fixed support. Labels indicate 'spring', 'mass', and 'scale'.

Parts.part_text: Explain how the mass causes a force on the spring.
The force on the spring is a vector quantity. State what is meant by a vector quantity.
Fig. 1.2 shows a graph of the length of the spring plotted against the force on the spring, for forces between 0 and 10N.

Question_text: Fig. 2.1 shows two engineers measuring the length of a wall made from concrete. The wall is 2.0m high, 15m long and 0.25 m thick. The weight of the wall is 180000N and the mass of the wall is 18000 kg.
image: Fig. 2.1 shows a rectangular concrete wall with two engineers. One engineer is at one end of the wall, and the other is at the other end, both appearing to measure its length. Dimensions are indicated: 2.0 m for height, 0.25 m for thickness, and 15 m for length. The image is marked as '(not to scale)'.

Parts.part_text: The engineers measure the length of the wall in one single measurement. State the name of the measuring instrument they use.
The engineers state that the density of the concrete affects the pressure exerted by the wall on the ground but that the length of the wall does not affect this pressure.

Question_text: Two different kettles are used to heat water, as shown in Fig. 3.1. Data for the two kettles is shown in Fig. 3.2.
image: Fig. 3.1 shows two types of kettles. On the left is an 'electric kettle', a standard electric jug-style kettle. On the right is a 'gas heated kettle' placed on top of a 'gas burner', a traditional stovetop kettle.

Parts.part_text: Data for the two kettles is shown in Fig. 3.2.
Parts.image: Fig. 3.2 is a table with two rows (electric kettle, gas heated kettle) and two columns (energy supplied to the kettle in one minute/J, thermal energy (heat) supplied by the kettle to the water in one minute/J). Parts.part_text: Both kettles contain the same mass of water, at the same initial temperature. State and explain which kettle brings the water to boiling point first.
The boiling water produces steam at 100°C. State one difference between molecules in the steam and molecules in the boiling water.

Question_text: A metal can and a plastic bottle, both containing liquid, are cooled by placing them in a jug of melting ice, as shown in Fig. 4.1. The can and bottle each contain 330 g of the same liquid at 15°C.
image: Fig. 4.1 shows a cross-section of a jug containing 'melting ice'. Inside the melting ice, there is a metal can and a plastic bottle, both containing liquid. The liquid in the can is shown as a grey cylinder, and the liquid in the bottle is shown as a light grey bottle shape.

Parts.part_text: The specific heat capacity of the liquid is 4.2J/(g°C). Calculate the thermal energy released when 330 g of the liquid at 15°C cools to 2°C.
When water at 0°C is used in the jug, instead of the melting ice, the cooling is slower. Explain why cooling is faster when using melting ice in the jug, rather than water at 0°C.
The liquid in the metal can cools down faster than the liquid in the plastic bottle. Suggest why this happens.

Question_text: When a balloon is rubbed on hair, the balloon becomes negatively charged. The balloon is shown in Fig. 5.1.
image: Fig. 5.1 shows a person holding a balloon that has been rubbed on their hair. The hair on their head is shown attracted towards the balloon, standing on end.

Parts.part_text: Explain how rubbing causes the balloon to become negatively charged.
Explain why the hair is pulled towards the balloon.
Explain why it is important that the balloon is made from an electrical insulator.
State one example where static electricity is useful.

Question_text: An electric hairdryer and an electric heater are connected to the mains supply, as shown in Fig. 7.1.
image: Fig. 7.1 shows a diagram of an electric hairdryer and an electric heater. Both appliances are connected via a mains plug to a wall socket, illustrating their connection to the mains supply.

Parts.part_text: The cable from the heater to the mains supply has a live, a neutral and an earth wire. State the purpose of the neutral wire.
The live wire in the electric heater touches the outer metal case. Explain how the earth and the fuse together protect the user from electric shock.
The hairdryer does not have an earth wire. Explain why this hairdryer is still safe to use.
In some modern homes, circuit breakers are used instead of fuses. Suggest one advantage of using a circuit breaker rather than a fuse.
